summary.essence: A tablet can retry a note after losing the response and receive its original receipt.
summary.problem: The tablet can lose its connection after the server saves a note. Sending the note again previously inserted a second copy.
summary.behaviorBefore: Every upload inserted a new note.
summary.behaviorAfter: The tablet sends a stable draft key. Once the server records its receipt, another upload with that key returns the first note ID.
unchanged: The response still contains the saved note ID.

groups.title: Give each draft a repeatable upload key
groups.essence: A retry sends the same saved draft ID as the first upload.

story.say: The upload includes the draft ID alongside the note text.

groups.title: Return the receipt on a later attempt
groups.essence: The server returns a known receipt and records the note ID after a new insert.

hunks.why: The test simulates a retry after the first write completes.

story.say: A matching receipt returns the earlier note ID.
On the first upload, the server inserts a note and then records its ID.
The test repeats a completed request and expects a single stored note.

findings.title: A failed receipt write leaves a duplicate on retry
findings.explanation: The note insert completes before the receipt is recorded. If the receipt write fails, the next attempt sees no key and inserts another note.
findings.suggestedDirection: Commit the note and its receipt in one transaction and exercise the gap between those writes.

findings.title: Which part of the request should carry the key?
findings.explanation: The API exports a receipt header name while the tablet sends the key in the body. Which contract should other clients follow?
